1. (Currently amended) A method comprising:
receiving requests and data records from a plurality of creditors to file bankruptcy documents with a plurality of different bankruptcy organizations, wherein the requests are specifically for filing proofs of claims for debts owed by debtors to the creditors;
automatically generating the bankruptcy documents with the received data records by transforming the data records into documents formatted according to the specific filing requirements of each different bankruptcy organization, wherein the bankruptcy documents are suitable for filing with different bankruptcy organizations; and
batch filing the bankruptcy documents with the different bankruptcy organizations by electronically submitting the formatted documents directly to each bankruptcy organization's filing system.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 wherein the different bankruptcy organizations are different courts with different filing system configurations, and wherein the automatically generating step includes determining the specific formatting requirements for each court and applying those requirements to generate court-specific bankruptcy documents.

6. (Currently amended) A method comprising:
receiving requests from a plurality of creditors to file proofs of claims for debts owed by debtors to the creditors with a plurality of different bankruptcy organizations, wherein each request includes a data record for generating a proof of claim;
automatically generating the proofs of claims with the received data records by transforming each data record into a proof of claim document formatted according to the specific filing requirements and rules of each different bankruptcy organization, wherein the proofs of claims are suitable for filing with different bankruptcy organizations; and
batch filing the proofs of claims with the different bankruptcy organizations by electronically submitting the formatted proofs of claims directly to each bankruptcy organization's designated filing system.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein the different bankruptcy organizations are different bankruptcy courts having different filing system configurations, and wherein the automatically generating step includes determining the specific proof of claim format and supporting documentation requirements for each court.

8. (Original) The method of claim 6 further comprising sending bankruptcy notification messages to the plurality of creditors, wherein the bankruptcy notification messages notify the creditors that various debtors have filed for bankruptcy.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein receiving requests from the plurality of creditors comprises receiving the requests using a secure file transfer protocol and validating the data records prior to generating the proofs of claims.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 wherein receiving requests comprises receiving requests via a Web site that includes validation and verification of creditor identity and authorization to file proofs of claims.

11. (Original) The method of claim 6 where batch filing comprises aggregating the proofs of claims and filing the proofs of claims in a batch mode at least once per day.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 further comprising:
generating a report that tracks the status of filed proofs of claims; and
sending the report to a particular creditor.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein generating the report comprises enabling a user to request the report using a Web site.

14. (Original) The method of claim 12 wherein generating the report comprises generating an aging report specifying a reason some proofs of claims have not been filed.

15. (Original) The method of claim 12 further comprising receiving a filing receipt for a filed proof of claim.

16. (Original) The method of claim 6 wherein batch filing is performed by a server computer.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6 further comprising validating the data record to ensure compliance with the filing requirements of the different bankruptcy organizations.
